statement.p: Find the directional derivative of f(x,y,z) = xz+y^{3}, at (1,2,3) in the direction of \vec v = \,\mathit{\vec i}+\,\mathit{\vec j}+\,\mathit{\vec k}.

static.solution:
\mbox{grad} f = z\,\mathit{\vec i}+3y^{2}\,\mathit{\vec j}+x\,\mathit{\vec k}, so \mbox{grad} f(1,2,3) = 3\,\mathit{\vec i}+12\,\mathit{\vec j}+\,\mathit{\vec k}.
A unit vector in the direction we want is u= \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}( \,\mathit{\vec i}+\,\mathit{\vec j}+\,\mathit{\vec k} ).
Therefore, the directional derivative is \mbox{grad} f(1,2,3) \cdot \vec u = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left( 3 + 12 + 1 \right) = \frac{16}{\sqrt{3}}.
